transcript.content: Hello, welcome in. I'm Dr. Smith. To start off, can you tell me what brings you in to see me today?

I guess… it’s work-related. I’m a translator, and for months I’ve been noticing the same pattern in project files. Certain subcontractors, and one colleague, keep making small changes to the translation memory and the timestamps so it looks like my quality control failed.

IT says the audit trail is clean, but… I don’t really buy that. The record looks arranged to put the blame on me.
How long have you been noticing this pattern and feeling that people are altering records to blame you—days, weeks, or longer?
Longer. About… eleven months, I think. It started not long after I was put in charge of that new localization project.
Have you ever heard voices or sounds that others couldn't hear, or seen things that others didn't see, during this time?
No… not really. I mean, I haven’t seen anything like that. It’s more about the records and the files, not… voices or things.
Aside from this situation at work, do you generally find yourself distrustful or suspicious of other people in your life—friends, family, or people you meet—even before this project started?
I don’t think so. I mean… I keep to myself, but I wouldn’t say I was suspicious of everyone before this. It’s mainly this work situation.

Outside of this situation with your coworkers and the records, have you noticed any changes in how you're managing daily life—like keeping up with chores, hygiene, or spending time with friends and family?

No, not much. I mean… I still do my translation work, keep the team’s workflow moving, pay the bills. At home the usual routines are still happening.

It’s really only when the file history comes up, or certain coworkers get involved, that things… go off track.
During these past eleven months, have you experienced any periods of unusually low mood, loss of interest in things, or conversely, elevated mood or unusually high energy?
I don’t think so. I’ve been stressed, sure, but not… depressed like that. And I haven’t had any period where I felt unusually energetic or anything.

When IT tells you the audit trail is clean, how do you respond internally—do you consider that they might be right, or do you remain completely certain that the records were tampered with regardless of what they find?

I try to consider it, but… no, not really. When IT says it’s clean, it just feels like they’re looking at the part that’s been made to look clean.

The pattern is still there in the project files—the little changes in the translation memory, the timestamps, the same subcontractors, and one colleague. It’s arranged so my quality control looks like the problem. So I don’t really accept that nothing happened.
Have you been using any recreational drugs, alcohol, or new medications during these past eleven months?
No… nothing new like that. I’m not using drugs, and alcohol isn’t really a thing for me. No new medications that I can think of.
